Tugboat – Nightfall

(79 Reviews)

Designed for cruising cities, neighborhoods and campuses, the Tugboat is compact but wide enough for a comfortable and smooth turning ride. A full-sized tail combined with a short but functional nose, creates a fun and functional skateboard.

KEY FEATURES

  • Wide platform – comfort and controlled turning.
  • Small Nose – keeps it compact.
  • Mellow Concave – comfort and relaxed riding.
  • Traditional Skate feel with more turn – Polar Bear 155mm trucks & soft 60mm Lil EZ Hawgs.
  • Built for – Cruising, carving, and exploring urban areas.
  • Great for – beginners learning basics or experts that want to cruise.
  • Artwork by Holls Walck.

$99.99 – $199.99Price range: $99.99 through $199.99

Clear
Clear
DESCRIPTION

A wider and slightly longer version of the Dinghy; the Tugboat comes in at 30″ long and 9.25″ wide. The wider platform is ideal for riders with larger feet who are looking for a comfortable cruiser board experience. The Tugboat is pressed with 7 plies of Canadian maple for a light, stiff and poppy ride. 60mm 83a Lil EZ Hawgs wheels finish off the setup and ensure you’ll have a smooth ride with plenty of roll speed and grip without having to worry about wheelbite.

SPECS
Length: 30″
Width: 9.24″
Wheelbase: 14.8″
Flex Rating: Stiff

(?)

FEATURES

Sanded Wheel Wells

Wheel wells are sanded into the board to expand wheel size compatability.

Medium Cave

The perfect middle ground, enough concave that you always feel glued to your board, but not too much to hurt your feet during a longer cruise.

Kicktail

Take your skating into the third dimension with a kicktail. We design our kicktails to work perfectly with each deck shape as well as with the truck and wheel setup on each complete.

100% Canadian Maple

Canadian Maple is a strong and proven material used in the world’s best skateboards. We source only the finest veneers found in Eastern Canada.

Made In North America

Proudly produced in North America.

SKATE SPOTS

Neighbourhood | Pathways | Campus | Rough Pavement | All Terrain

COMPONENTS

TRUCKS

Polar Bear 155mm

SEE DETAILS

Designed with time-tested geometry and engineered with high quality materials, the 155mm Polar Bears are going to be exactly what you need if you’re going to hit the skatepark, slappy curb or just about any other obstacle. Sold in pairs. Bushings: 93a

WHEELS

60mm Lil EZs

SEE DETAILS

The 60mm Lil EZ Slides bring all the sliding power of their 63mm counterpart into a compact, lightweight design, making them an excellent choice for riders who want ultimate versatility. Their 83a durometer ensures effortless, controlled slides, whether you’re freeriding, downhill sliding, or experimenting with technical tricks.

BEARINGS

SPACEBALLS

SEE DETAILS

 Spaceballs are our answer to all of your bearing problems.  Never again can you lose your washers, or spacers because we’ve built them into the inner race!  On the functional side, this means your bearings are always mated correctly which negates any bearing-induced chatter.

Tugboat - Atmosphere
SlimHouseUA
Rating: 5/5
Awesome cruiser
After a few weeks of riding, I can confidently say the Landyachtz Tugboat is an awesome board for city cruising. It feels super stable and roomy underfoot, yet still nimble enough to weave through people and dodge cracks or potholes with ease. Before this, I was riding a Santa Cruz 27.7”, so the Tugboat is slightly bigger — but that extra size is actually a plus. It offers better foot placement and more confidence overall. The deck smooths out vibrations nicely, with just a bit of flex, which makes rough pavement a lot more forgiving. It does take a little time to get used to the feel and weight, but once you do, it flows naturally. The only thing I’d change are the wheels. The stock hawgs are fine, but I’m planning to swap them out for 63mm Doozies for a smoother, grippier ride — especially over cobblestone and rougher roads. As expected from Landyachtz, the build quality is top-notch. The trucks came well-tuned out of the box, the grip is solid, and the deck looks and feels great. If I were picking my first cruiser board again, I’d absolutely go with the Tugboat.

Flex Ratings

We’ve categorized the stiffness of our boards into 3 main groups, listed below.  The general rule is the faster you’re skating, the stiffer the deck, but this is not universal.

 

Flexy – Soft and supple flex profile best suited for carving and cruising on longer boards. The bouncy nature of these decks lets you turn deeper and surf your surrounds.

 

Medium – The do it all of our boards, a perfect balance of stability and carve.

 

Stiff – From cruisers to downhill boards a stiff flex profile excels in stability and responsiveness.  Whether you’re dipping into driveways or bombing a mountain pass you’ll be down with the stiffness.
